# Continuous integration

`workflows/ci.yml` runs on pull requests, default-branch pushes, and manual dispatches. Every check is its own job and the jobs run in parallel, so a run takes as long as its slowest check. A newer push to a pull request cancels its run in progress; master pushes run to the end so the deploy is never cancelled. All CI helpers run with Bun, pinned by `.bun-version`.

Actions are pinned to commit SHAs. Dependabot checks for action updates weekly.

Bun jobs run the root `lint:ci`, `typecheck`, `test`, and `build` scripts, one job each, with a 5-minute timeout. Each takes seconds, so they start at once and run on every change, with no change detection in front of them. `lint:ci` checks oxlint, oxfmt and the generated Swift schema without writing. `.bun-version` and `packageManager` pin Bun; update them together. Commit `bun.lock` after changing dependencies. CI caches package downloads, then always installs with `--frozen-lockfile`.

The pre-commit hook (`lefthook.yml`) already ran the fixers, the type check, the schema check, the server tests and `swift test` before the commit existed. CI repeats them for what a hook can't see: a merge, a machine without the hook, and the builds. A CI failure the hook could have caught is a hook bug, so fix the hook. A new check is a package script first. Add it to the hook if it finishes in seconds, and to the `task` matrix as its own job.

The app never runs env-manager in CI. The committed readers (`env.ts`) and `Config/check-env.sh` validate the environment. Bun loads the tracked `.env` defaults for scripts run from the repository root, and the Swift jobs name the two settings Xcode needs in their `env:`, because `Config/Base.xcconfig` includes the generated xcconfig files only when they exist. Keep defaults harmless and complete enough for CI. Never commit `.env.local` or native local secrets, and never cache environment outputs.

Swift runs as two jobs that never boot a simulator. `package` runs `swift test` on macOS, which compiles the app's sources and runs the logic tests. `app` builds the shared `App` Xcode scheme in Release for a generic iOS simulator without signing. Both wait for the `changes` job, which reads the diff so that they take a macOS runner only when native inputs changed: anything outside `server/` and `wrangler.jsonc`, docs excepted. Otherwise each reports success from a Linux runner, which keeps a required check green. Manual dispatches and initial pushes run them. Edit `scripts/changes.ts` when the layout changes. A failure in change detection fails the Swift jobs too. Native jobs run on GitHub's `xcode-27` image with its installed Xcode and Swift, and cache only package dependencies with a key including both toolchain versions. `Package.resolved` is untracked: each Swift task first runs `scripts/own-packages.ts`, which moves the owner's own packages to their branch's head, and the package cache is saved per run so a run that can't reach GitHub builds the previous run's packages.

The Worker deploys from a master push once every check passed. `workflows/testflight.yml` uploads a TestFlight build on master pushes that touch the app.
